summary: The Torah sets a fine (kenas) that a man must pay when he harms a young girl. This mishnah lists girls who get the fine even though they were forbidden to him.

chunks.en: These are the girls who get a kenas (fine):
chunks.st: These are the cases of young women for whom there is a fine paid to their fathers by one who rapes them:

words.note: A fine the Torah sets for a man who harms a young girl.

chunks.en: one who sins with a mamzeres,
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with a mamzeret,

chunks.st: or with a Gibeonite woman [netina],
chunks.stMore: who are given [netunim] to the service of the people and the altar (see Joshua 9:27),

chunks.en: or with a Kusis.
chunks.st: or with a Samaritan woman [kutit].

words.note: A girl from the Kusim, who lived in Shomron.

chunks.explain: When beis din punishes with death, there is no fine.
chunks.st: there is no court-imposed capital punishment.
chunks.stMore: In cases where there is a court-imposed death penalty, the rapist would be exempt from paying the fine.

summary: A young girl had erusin and was divorced, and then a man harmed her. Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says she gets no kenas; Rabbi Akiva says she gets it, and it is hers, not her father's.

chunks.en: A young girl who had erusin and was divorced,
chunks.st: a young woman who was betrothed and divorced, and then raped,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: she gets no kenas.
chunks.st: She does not receive payment of a fine for her rape.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: she gets a kenas,
chunks.st: She receives payment of a fine for her rape

chunks.en: and her kenas is for herself.
chunks.st: and her fine is paid to herself,
chunks.stMore: not her father, as since she was betrothed and divorced she is no longer subject to her father’s authority.

summary: A man who tricked a girl pays three kinds of payment, and one who forced her pays four. The mishnah lists the differences between them.

chunks.en: The one who tricks a girl pays three things,
chunks.st: The seducer gives the father of his victim three things,

chunks.en: and the one who forces her pays four.
chunks.st: and the rapist gives the father four.

chunks.en: The one who tricks pays for shame, for damage, and the kenas.
chunks.st: The mishna specifies: The seducer gives the father payments for humiliation, degradation, and the fine.

chunks.en: The one who forces adds to that,
chunks.st: A rapist adds an addition to his payments,

chunks.en: that he pays for the pain.
chunks.st: as he also gives payment for the pain.

chunks.en: What is the difference between them?
chunks.st: What are the differences between the halakha of a rapist and that of a seducer?

chunks.en: The one who forces pays for the pain,
chunks.st: The rapist gives payment for the pain,

chunks.en: and the one who tricks does not pay for the pain.
chunks.st: and the seducer does not give payment for the pain.

chunks.en: The one who forces pays right away,
chunks.st: The rapist gives payment immediately,

chunks.en: and the one who tricks pays only if he sends her away.
chunks.st: and the seducer does not pay those payments immediately but only when he releases her.

chunks.en: The one who forces must drink from his own pot,
chunks.explain: He must marry her and may never send her away.
chunks.st: The rapist drinks from his vessel [atzitzo], i.e., marries the woman he raped, perforce,

chunks.en: and the one who tricks may send her away if he wants.
chunks.st: and the seducer, if he wishes to release her, he releases her.

summary: The one who forced a girl must marry her and keep her, even if she has a handicap. But if she is forbidden to him, he may not stay married to her.

chunks.en: What does drink from his own pot mean?
chunks.st: How does the rapist drink from his vessel?

chunks.en: Even if she is lame,
chunks.st: Even if the woman he raped is lame,

chunks.en: even if she is blind,
chunks.st: even if she is blind,

chunks.en: and even if she has boils, he must keep her.
chunks.st: and even if she is afflicted with boils,
chunks.stMore: he is obligated to marry her and may not divorce her.

chunks.en: But if she did a forbidden thing,
chunks.st: However, if a matter of licentiousness is found in her, e.g., if she committed adultery,

chunks.en: or she is not allowed to marry a Jew,
chunks.st: or if she is unfit to enter the Jewish people, e.g., if she is a mamzeret,

chunks.en: he may not keep her,
chunks.st: he is not permitted to sustain her as his wife,

chunks.en: as it says (Devarim 22), And she shall be his wife,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And to him she shall be as a wife”
chunks.stMore: (Deuteronomy 22:29), from which it is inferred that she must be

chunks.en: a wife who is fit for him.
chunks.st: a woman who is legally suitable for him.

summary: An orphan girl had erusin and was divorced. Rabbi Elazar says that one who tricked her does not pay the kenas, but one who forced her does.

chunks.en: An orphan girl who had erusin and was divorced,
chunks.st: an orphan who was betrothed and divorced,

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: the one who tricks her is free, and the one who forces her must pay.
chunks.explain: She agreed, and she is in charge of herself.
chunks.st: One who rapes her is obligated to pay the fine, as she is a virgin young woman, and one who seduces her is exempt
chunks.stMore: from payment. Because she is an orphan, or because she was betrothed and divorced, she is independent, and by consenting to the seduction she forgoes her right to the fine.

summary: The payment for shame depends on who caused it and who was shamed. The damage is measured like the price of a maidservant, and the kenas is the same for everyone.

chunks.en: What is shame?
chunks.st: What is humiliation?
chunks.stMore: How is the payment for humiliation during rape or seduction assessed?

chunks.en: It all depends on who shamed and who was shamed.
chunks.st: It is all based on the one who humiliated and the one who was humiliated.
chunks.stMore: The price will vary depending on the lineage of the family of the rape victim and the nature of the attacker.

words.en: and the one who is shamed

chunks.he: פְּגָם, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא שִׁפְחָה נִמְכֶּרֶת,
chunks.en: Damage: we look at her as if she were a maidservant being sold,
chunks.st: How is her degradation assessed? One considers her as though she were a maidservant sold in the marketplace,

chunks.en: how much she was worth before, and how much she is worth now.
chunks.st: and assesses how much she was worth beforehand and how much she is currently worth, after the rape or seduction.

chunks.en: The kenas is the same for every person.
chunks.st: The sum of the fine is equal for all people,

chunks.en: And anything that has a set amount from the Torah
chunks.st: and the principle is: Any payment that has a fixed sum by Torah law

chunks.en: is the same for every person.
chunks.st: is equal for all people,
chunks.stMore: regardless of the lineage and the physical state of the attacker or the victim.

summary: A father may sell his very young daughter as a maidservant, and then there is no kenas. A young girl gets the kenas and cannot be sold, and an older girl gets neither.

chunks.en: Wherever there is selling,
chunks.explain: A father may sell his young daughter as a maidservant.
chunks.st: Any place where there is sale
chunks.stMore: by a father of his minor daughter as a Hebrew maidservant,

chunks.en: there is no kenas.
chunks.st: there is no fine if she is raped.

chunks.en: And wherever there is a kenas,
chunks.st: And any place where there is a fine, when a young woman is raped;

chunks.en: there is no selling.
chunks.st: there is no sale by the father.

chunks.en: A little girl can be sold
chunks.st: The Gemara specifies: A minor is subject to sale by her father,

chunks.en: and does not get a kenas.
chunks.st: and she is not entitled to a fine if she is raped.

chunks.en: A young girl gets a kenas
chunks.st: A young woman is entitled to a fine if she is raped

chunks.en: and cannot be sold.
chunks.st: and is not subject to sale.

chunks.en: A grown-up girl has neither
chunks.st: A grown woman is neither

chunks.en: selling nor kenas.
chunks.st: subject to sale nor entitled to a fine.

summary: A man who admits to a wrong pays the normal payment, but not a fine. A fine, which is more than the damage, is paid only when witnesses prove it.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר פִּתִּיתִי אֶת בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי,

chunks.st: One who says: I seduced the daughter of so-and-so,

chunks.en: pays for shame and damage because he admitted it,
chunks.st: pays compensation for humiliation and degradation based on his own admission,

chunks.en: but he does not pay the kenas.
chunks.st: but does not pay the fine.

chunks.en: One who says, I stole, and slaughtered, and sold,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who says: I stole,

chunks.en: pays the value of what he stole because he admitted it,
chunks.st: pays the principal, the value of the stolen goods, based on his own admission,

chunks.st: but does not pay the double payment and

chunks.en: or four or five times as much.
chunks.st: the payment four and five

chunks.en: If he says, My ox killed so-and-so,

chunks.st: My ox killed an ox belonging to so-and-so,

chunks.en: he pays because he admitted it.
chunks.st: this owner pays based on his own admission.

chunks.st: However, if he said: My ox killed a slave belonging to so-and-so,

chunks.en: he does not pay because he admitted it.
chunks.st: he does not pay based on his own admission as that payment is a fine.

chunks.en: This is the rule: anyone who pays
chunks.st: This is the principle: Anyone who pays

chunks.en: more than the damage he did
chunks.st: more than what he damaged,

chunks.en: does not pay because he admitted it.
chunks.st: the payments are fines and therefore he does not pay based on his own
chunks.stMore: admission. He pays only based on the testimony of others.
